books.section: America in an Era of Turmoil (1960–1975)

options.text: The War Powers Resolution’s attempt to limit presidential war-making power

options.misconception: Vietnam led to the repeal of all congressional authority over foreign policy.
options.text: The repeal of all congressional authority over foreign policy

options.misconception: Vietnam led to a permanent military draft without end.
options.text: The establishment of a permanent military draft without end

options.misconception: Vietnam led to the end of all U.S. alliances in Asia.
options.text: The end of all U.S. alliances in Asia

rationales.A: Background: the War Powers Resolution of 1973 tried to reassert congressional limits on presidential war-making after Vietnam. It required the president to consult Congress and to withdraw troops after sixty days without approval.
rationales.B: Congress sought more authority over war, not less; the repeal of its authority is the reverse.
rationales.C: The draft ended; no permanent draft without end was established.
rationales.D: Asian alliances continued; they did not end.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what Vietnam taught about presidential war-making. A president had taken the country deep into war.
2. Name the response. Background: the War Powers Resolution of 1973 tried to limit presidential war-making power.
3. Test the reversals. Congress sought more authority, the draft ended, and alliances continued.
4. Match the change. A law limiting the president is the direct result of the Vietnam experience.
Remember: a war that expands presidential power often produces a law to pull it back.

source: original; stimulus is a paraphrase of Lyndon B. Johnson’s addresses on Vietnam (1964–1965)
stem: Which of the following later developments best illustrates a change resulting from the Vietnam War experience?

stimulus.source_note: Lyndon B. Johnson, address on Vietnam, 1964–1965, paraphrased from presidential addresses.
stimulus.text: We can continue to help the people of South Vietnam to defend their freedom or we can abandon them. I have chosen to continue our commitment to the freedom of South Vietnam.
